summary: This scenario covers a billing cycle where the cardholder makes purchases within the credit limit, receives a statement, and then makes a payment after the due date that is also less than the required minimum. It is designed to probe the late-payment path, including failure to satisfy the minimum payment obligation by the due date while still keeping the account under the credit limit.
assumptions: The previous statement had a nonzero carried balance, so the grace-period clause is relevant and is not satisfied because the account was not paid in full by the prior due date.
The account remains below the disclosed credit limit throughout the scenario, so the credit-limit obligation is performed rather than breached.
The statement's minimum payment is calculated under the contract formula as 3% of the new balance or $15, whichever is greater; for a $650.00 new balance, the minimum payment is $19.50.
The late payment posts through an approved standard payment channel and is credited on its receipt date.

A payment made after the due date and below the minimum does not cure the missed on-time minimum-payment obligation for this statement period; the archetype therefore treats the minimum-payment obligation as unmet by the deadline.

The grace-period obligation is represented with a bound event for executor matching, but in this archetype it is treated as unmet because the account was not paid in full within the applicable grace-period conditions.

metadata.note: Beginning of cycle reflects carried previous balance; grace-period avoidance condition will not be met for new purchases in this cycle.
Late payment posted after due date and below required minimum.
Account follows late-payment path because no qualifying minimum payment was made by 2025-03-25 and the later payment was only $10.00.
